headline: California Governor Gavin Newsom called the White House's voluntary AI accord reckless and said his state will speed up its own AI rules.
score_reason: Sharp but days-old remarks (30 Sep) reported again on 4 Oct with no new action; lowered from 6 for staleness.
importance_line: Californians, and the AI companies based there, may face state rules sooner because Newsom says Washington has left the field, but the only concrete step so far is a review group whose recommendations are not yet written.
summary: Benzinga reports, in a piece carried by Yahoo News, that California Governor Gavin Newsom wrote on X on 30 Sep 2026 that the White House's voluntary AI accord was "like Big Pharma saying we don't need the FDA" and that President Trump's "let it rip" approach is "RECKLESS". Newsom said California must "accelerate our timelines" on AI regulation in the absence of federal leadership and that an independent group created by his executive order will report recommendations the state plans to adopt; the accord he mocked is a non-binding pact signed by Trump and the heads of Alphabet, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI and Nvidia.
notes: Source is Benzinga (text carried by Yahoo); Benzinga URL not available, so the Yahoo page is linked. Underlying post dated Wednesday 30 Sep 2026.
